about: The public pay floor law's starting row. The series is a salary floor a government sets that binds its own employers and every level under it (src/core2/data/laws/public-pay-floor.json). No such law is in force in any of the 56 places: each government pays its own staff by its own schedule (the federal General Schedule, state civil service plans, city and county charters), which the jobs engine's role rates already carry, and the floor every public employer must pay is the minimum wage (its own series), which covers federal, state and local public employees alike. So the floor starts at 0 (none) at the federal level and binds nothing until a body enacts one.

rows.source: 29 U.S.C. 203(e)(2) and (x) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/29/203): the Fair Labor Standards Act's minimum wage covers 'any individual employed by a State, political subdivision of a State, or an interstate governmental agency' and 'any individual employed by the Government of the United States'; Garcia v. San Antonio Metropolitan Transit Authority, 469 U.S. 528 (February 19, 1985) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/469/528), upheld 'affording SAMTA employees the protections of the wage and hour provisions of the FLSA'; 5 U.S.C. 5332(a)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/5/5332): 'Each employee to whom this subchapter applies is entitled to basic pay in accordance with the General Schedule', a schedule for federal staff only.
rows.note: No law sets one salary floor for every public job at a level and the levels under it; 0 means none.
